songInfo.title: Man in the Box
songInfo.tuning: Half-Step Down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

scalesUsed.notes: Eb - Gb - Ab - Bb - Db - Eb
scalesUsed.application: Played in open E minor position on a guitar tuned half-step down (E - G - A - B - D shapes) for the main talk-box riff and Jerry Cantrell's solo

scalesUsed.notes: Eb - Gb - Ab - A - Bb - Db - Eb
scalesUsed.application: Adds the gritty flat-5th passing tone during the chorus fills and solo bends

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Sludgy Seattle grunge minor-pentatonic grind contrasted with a bright bIII - bVII - IV (G - D - A shapes) chorus chord explosion
keyAndScale.keySignature: 6 flats (played as 1 sharp E minor shapes in Eb standard tuning)
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: Eb minor is the relative minor of Gb major

mainProgression.progressionDescription: Played in Eb standard tuning using E5, G, D, and A chord shapes: the verse grinds on a hypnotic E minor pentatonic riff while the chorus erupts into a massive bIII - bVII - IV - i cadence.
mainProgression.description: Played in Eb standard tuning using E5, G, D, and A chord shapes: the verse grinds on a hypnotic E minor pentatonic riff while the chorus erupts into a massive bIII - bVII - IV - i cadence.

sectionProgressions.section: Intro & Verse Riff ('I'm the man in the box')
sectionProgressions.description: Chugging open low-E pedal riff punctuated by talk-box/wah pentatonic hooks and a brief C#5 pre-chorus dip

sectionProgressions.section: Chorus ('Feed my eyes, can you sew them shut?')
sectionProgressions.description: Towering power-chord/open-chord descent supporting Layne Staley's legendary vocal wail
Jerry Cantrell's fiery E minor pentatonic / blues solo combining wah-inflected bends with rapid legato flurries
Open-position E minor pentatonic grunge riff and bend drill

harmonicFunction: E5 (i) - Heavy low-string pedal tonic (sounding as Eb5 in half-step down tuning)
G5 (bIII) - Mediant lift that launches the soaring chorus
D5 (bVII) - Subtonic chord stepping down from G5 with dark grandeur
A5 (IV) - Dorian-borrowed major IV / power chord creating a stark plagal-style pull back into E5

techniques.name: Sludgy Low-String Pedal Riffing & Minor Pentatonic Bends
techniques.description: Alternating palm-muted open 6th-string chugs with bluesy 5th- and 4th-string pentatonic double-stops and quarter-tone bends

sequence: Tune all strings down a half step (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb) so open E5 sounds as concert Eb5
Anchor the main riff with palm-muted open low-E chugs between fretted notes on the 5th and 4th strings (frets 5 and 7)
Add a slight microtonal curl on the 3rd fret of the low E string (G note) at the end of the riff cycle
Open up into full, unmuted G, D, A5, and E5 chords when the chorus hits
tips: Don't rush the 107 BPM groove—Alice in Chains' heaviness comes from playing slightly behind the beat
If you don't own a talk box, a Dunlop Cry Baby wah pedal rocked in sync with the riff gets 90% of the vibe
Keep unused strings muted with your fretting hand when playing under high-gain distortion

sections.name: Main Talk-Box & Pentatonic Riff
sections.description: Jerry Cantrell's monolithic E minor pentatonic riff (in Eb tuning) built around the 5th and 7th frets.
notes: Palm-mute the open 6th-string pedal notes between the fretted 5th/4th string notes
Give the 3rd fret on the 6th string a gritty quarter-step blues bend
Lock your right hand into the heavy drum groove

sections.name: Chorus ('Feed My Eyes')
sections.description: Massive four-chord chorus progression moving through G5, D5, A5, and E5.
notes: Let G5 and D5 ring out with full sustain for half a bar each
Hit A5 and resolve into the open E5 riff turnaround
Add the bluesy 3rd-string 2nd-fret bend fill over the E5 resolution

sections.name: Scale Practice Exercise
sections.description: E minor blues/pentatonic lead lick in 12th and open position inspired by Jerry Cantrell's solo.
notes: Attack each note firmly with the pick and add wide rock vibrato
Include the flat-5th blue note (5th string 6th fret / 3rd string 3rd fret) for extra grit
Sweep your wah pedal forward as you ascend into the high register

guitar.recommended: G&L Rampage or Gibson Les Paul Studio (tuned down 1/2 step to Eb)
guitar.pickup: High-output bridge humbucker (Seymour Duncan JB style)

amp.recommended: Bogner Fish Preamp / Modified Marshall JCM800
alternatives: Friedman BE-OD Pedal into clean amp

effects.other: Heil Talk Box (for authentic intro/verse vowel sweep) or Dunlop Cry Baby Wah

beginner.title: Chorus Chords & Simplified Verse Riff
steps: Practice the G5 - D5 - A5 - E5 chorus changes at 85 BPM
Learn the single-note outline of the main verse riff on the 6th, 5th, and 4th strings
Play through the verse and chorus structure at 107 BPM

intermediate.title: Palm-Muted Pedal Riff & Wah/Talk-Box Inflection
steps: Integrate tight open-E palm muting between the 5th- and 7th-fret riff notes
Add the C#5 - D5 pre-chorus transition and chorus blues fills
Coordinate a wah pedal with the main riff and solo phrases

advanced.title: Full Jerry Cantrell Solo & Microtonal Bends
steps: Master the complete guitar solo including rapid pentatonic legato bursts and unison bends
Nail the heavy behind-the-beat pocket throughout the entire track
Perform in half-step down tuning with zero unwanted string noise

commonMistakes: Playing the verse riff too fast and losing the heavy, stomping 107 BPM pocket
Forgetting to mute the open 6th string when switching to the fretted 5th and 4th strings
Over-bending the 3rd-fret G note on the low E string so it goes out of tune
practiceRoutine: 3 minutes: Palm-muted open E string to 5th/7th fret string-skipping drill
4 minutes: Main verse riff loop with quarter-step 3rd-fret bend
4 minutes: G5 → D5 → A5 → E5 chorus transitions with lead turnaround fill
4 minutes: Minor blues solo improvisation over the chorus progression
focusAreas: Precision string muting under high gain
Expressive blues bends and wah pedal control
metronomeWork: Start the main riff at 85 BPM to lock in the syncopated 6th-string pedal notes
Increase to 96 BPM while adding wah pedal movement
Play at album tempo of 107 BPM sitting firmly in the back of the pocket
